title: Independent set algorithms from tropical circuit size
formal: Do there exist one deterministic Turing machine A and constants \(C,c\ge 1\) such that for every finite simple graph G on \(n\ge 1\) vertices and nonnegative integer weight vector w, A outputs the maximum independent-set weight within \(C(\tau (G)+n+\mathrm{L}+1)^{c}\) bit operations, where L is the total binary encoding length of w and \(\tau (G)\) is the minimum size of a tropical MWIS circuit defined below? Only G and w are supplied; neither \(\tau (G)\) nor a circuit is part of the input.
definitions: G is given by its \(n\times n\) adjacency matrix. The n nonnegative weights are binary integers with delimiters, all counted in L. A vertex set I is independent when no edge has both endpoints in I. \(MWIS(G,w)=\max\)_{I independent}\(\sum_{v\in I}w_{v}\), allowing \(I=\varnothing\) with weight zero. A tropical circuit for G is a finite acyclic circuit with one designated output, arbitrary fan-out, input gates labeled \(x_{v}\) or the constant 0, and binary internal gates labeled max or + with their ordinary real-number meanings. No other constants or operations are allowed. Size counts every gate, including input and constant gates. An MWIS circuit must output \(MWIS(G,x)\) for every vector \(x\in R_{\ge}0^{n}\), so its topology depends only on G. Define \(\tau (G)\) as the minimum size of such a circuit. This minimum exists because finitely many independent sets can each be summed and their maximum computed. The output algorithm may use general deterministic computation, not only tropical operations. Constants C,c are uniform over all graphs and weight vectors.
answer_criterion: Prove the proposition in the problem statement or its logical negation with the stated model, hypotheses and quantifier order. The proof must settle the entire target. A result conditional on an additional assumption settles only that conditional version. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete proof checked by a proof assistant and matching this statement.
why: Determine whether small nonuniform dynamic programs can always be exploited by a uniform exact algorithm without being supplied as certificates.

importance.reason: A general algorithm-versus-representation question connecting graph structure, dynamic programming and automatization beyond one decomposition family.

references.locator: Section 2.2, Definition 6 and Lemma 7; Corollary 4 on restricted-class automatization
references.title: Lower Bounds on Dynamic Programming for Maximum Weight Independent Set
Open problems: Can dynamic programming for independent set be automated?

progress.text: Korhonen proves tropical-circuit lower bounds and polynomial-overhead circuit construction on bounded-degree and fixed-minor-free graph classes.
The current list asks for polynomial or quasipolynomial runtime relative to optimal circuit size on arbitrary weighted graphs.

context_blocks.text: A small tropical circuit describes a compact computation of the optimum for every assignment of weights to a fixed graph. Knowing that this description exists does not immediately provide an algorithm for discovering or exploiting it.

The source paper fixes binary max and addition gates and the constant zero. It proves restricted-class automatization results; arbitrary graphs are the issue here. Correctness for all nonnegative weights and for all real weights give polynomially equivalent size parameters, as discussed in Section 2.2.

This card selects the polynomial target from the author’s polynomial-or-quasipolynomial question and measures actual bit cost. It asks to compute the optimum, rather than requiring the algorithm to output a circuit.

sentences: A tropical circuit combines vertex weights using only maximum and addition.
For each graph, \(\tau\) measures the smallest circuit that computes maximum independent-set weight for every nonnegative weight assignment.
The question asks for a uniform algorithm whose runtime is polynomial in \(\tau\) and the input size.
The algorithm receives no circuit or decomposition and may use unrestricted deterministic computation.
A positive answer would turn the existence of a compact dynamic program into an effective algorithmic guarantee.

status_note: Reviewed through 11 September 2026. The current author list retains general automatization as open; the 2021 positive results are restricted to bounded-degree or fixed-minor-free classes.

notes: Specified zero as the only constant and counted input gates. Kept the approved nonnegative-weight size parameter; the source’s all-real-weight parameter differs by at most a linear circuit overhead, so polynomial automatization is preserved.
statement_review.scope: Individual mathematical formulation and source review; not a proof-assistant formalization or verification of the cited proofs.
